This one’s not for the claustrophobic. Cave Challenge is a map like no other: [b]a tight space, a bunch of slot machines, and nowhere to run[/b]. Rack up a high score with your friends, or see how long you can survive in Nightmare mode.

Thanks to those who have been here from day one, thanks to those who joined along the way[/b]. Shoutout to our High Rollers and to everyone who’s covered this passion project of mine.

notes.title: The Visual Update is OUT NOW!
notes.content:
[h2]Dear Survivors,[/h2]

[h3]Your Halloween candy has arrived early. Hellbreach: Vegas is flashier, prettier, and scarier than ever. [/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43190635/f283212ac15755569882ce577250bd71c1b1ccaa.png[/img]
[h3]The Visual Update is [b]OUT NOW![/b][/h3]

I’ve already given you a little sneak preview of the updated slots, perk machines, and the terrifyingly refreshing new demon designs in last week’s blog. [b]Now, you can finally dive into the new visuals yourselves.[/b]

Here’s a list of the changes that you can expect once you boot up Hellbreach: 

[b]Upgraded Slot Machine Design:[/b] I revamped the slot machines with a more polished look and style that better fits the Vegas theme.

[b]Reworked Perks System:[/b] Perks can now be bought at a vending machine rather than from perk cards, providing a more cohesive and immersive experience.

[b]Polished Maps:[/b] I enhanced the maps where necessary, with improved models, textures, and overall layout refinements.

[b]Improved Lighting:[/b] The lighting has been improved across all maps for better atmosphere and visibility.

[b]Reworked Textures:[/b] All textures, including those for enemies, weapons, and environmental assets have been reworked.

[b]Updated Player Select Screen:[/b] I’ve revised the player selection interface for some additional polish.

[b]Enhanced Map and Enemy Visibility:[/b] The overall visibility of maps and enemies has been improved to make enemy visuals clearer and more distinguishable.

[b]Improved Enemy Damage and Death VFX:[/b] I implemented upgraded visual effects for enemy damage and deaths to make them more impactful.

[b]Smoothing of Enemy and Weapon Animations:[/b] Enemy and weapon animations are now smoother to improve fluidity in combat.

[b]Overall Optimization for Stable Frame Rates:[/b] I’ve enhanced performance across the board to achieve stable frame rates across various setups.
I’m really happy with how this update turned out and I can’t wait to see everybody’s reactions. 

If updated visuals sound enticing to you and you haven’t had the chance to pick up Hellbreach yet, the game will be 33% off during Steam’ Scream Fest. If you want to go for a test drive, the Hellbreach Demo has also been updated with the new visuals!

Now go play those freshly painted slots, will you?

notes.title: The First Look: Hellbreach: Vegas Visual Update
notes.content:
[h3]Dear Survivors,[/h3]

A week has passed since the last blog and, as promised, I’m here to share [b]a first look at the Hellbreach: Vegas Visual Update[/b] that we’ve been cooking up!

As mentioned in the previous blog, we’ll be rolling out a visual overhaul of [b]perks, slot machines, and our favourite slaying targets: demons![/b] So, let’s get into some of these changes:

[u][b]Slot machines[/b][/u]

The slot machines will maintain their trusty, one-armed bandit look - but with a [b]fresh coat of paint[/b]. Perk cards can now be bought using [b]soda vending machines[/b] that you can find spread out across the map. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43190635/587387d301b3b7f90b9a0238b8c53b5b243a37e8.png[/img]

I felt like redesigning the machines was a necessary step after some of your feedback made it clear they needed more polish and character to really match the "Vegas" vibe. The goal was to give them that flashy, over-the-top look while keeping the dark tone of the game. 

[u][b]Enemies[/b][/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43190635/2c004922f2f2dd4870bf779aaa42d2055cc1c891.png[/img]

Along with the machines, the demons will also be getting a visual upgrade! With[b] better textures and improved visibility[/b], you’ll still recognise their ugly mugs. But I added [b]a hellish glow and more detail that’ll make them stand out better in the game[/b], and make it more satisfying for you to watch them go [b]POP[/b]!

That’s all I want to show you for now! I’m really excited to consistently get to work on making Hellbreach fit my vision even closer and I’m glad that I have your feedback to guide me!

[b]What do you think of these changes? Are you looking forward to the visual update?[/b]

notes.title: Hellbreach: Vegas - Pre 1.0 Launch FAQ!
notes.content:
[h3]Dear Survivors,[/h3]

With the 1.0 release of Hellbreach: Vegas on our doorstep, we figured that some of you might still have some burning questions - as always, you can hop on our Discord or our Discussion page and ask away! 

But we thought it would make sense to do away with some of them in an FAQ blog!

[h5]What is the exact release date of the game?[/h5]
[b]August 14th, 2024, 5pm CEST / 8pm PT[/b]. Be there or be square!

[h5]What platforms will the game be available on?[/h5]
The game will be available on [b]Steam[/b].

[h5]Will the Leaderboards be reset upon 1.0 launch?[/h5]
Yes! As the game has gone through multiple balance changes we want to give [b]everyone a fair shot at the top of the leaderboards.
[/b]
[h5]What is the difference between the Early Access version of the game and the 1.0?[/h5]
The 1.0 release includes several [b]significant enhancements and additions[/b]. It features more maps, game modes, accessories, and weapons, offering a richer and more diverse gaming experience. Improved controller mechanics provide [b]a smoother and more intuitive gameplay experience[/b]. [b]Upgraded enemy AI and animations[/b] make the game more challenging and visually appealing. Additionally, the game has undergone [b]extensive refinement[/b], addressing bugs, optimizing performance, and improving visual and audio elements to deliver a more polished final product. These updates collectively ensure a more complete, immersive, and enjoyable game in the 1.0 version compared to the Early Access version.

[h5]What is the game's storyline or premise?[/h5]
On what seems like an ordinary night in the glowing city of Las Vegas, portals from hell suddenly open across the city, unleashing demonic hordes. The origins of these portals are shrouded in mystery, but it is speculated that the demons are harnessing the vibrant neon lights of Vegas as a power source for their home dimension: Hell. Vegas, famously known as Sin City, is an ideal refuge for these malevolent beings. As the city falls into chaos, you find yourself trapped with a group of survivors. Together, [b]you must fend off the relentless hordes of demons[/b] and uncover the truth behind the invasion while fighting for your lives in a city overrun by darkness.

[h5]Is there controller and/or Steam Deck support?[/h5]
The 1.0 release of the game has [b]full controller support[/b] and is [b]Steam Deck Compatible[/b]! 

[h5]How does the difficulty in the game scale?[/h5]
The game's difficulty [b]scales in several ways[/b]. As waves progress, demons become significantly stronger, faster and with increased health and faster spawning rates making them more challenging to evade and defeat. To survive, it's crucial to [b]continually upgrade your weapons[/b] to keep pace with the escalating difficulty.

[h5]What game engine is this build on?[/h5]
The game is built in [b]Unreal Engine 4[/b].

[h5]Who would win in a fight? Zombies or demons?[/h5]

notes.title: How The Crossbow in Hellbreach: Vegas is Tuned
notes.content:
[h2]Dear survivors,[/h2]

As you might have noticed, there’s a new addition in the Hellbreach arsenal. And it packs a punch: [b]Say hi to the crossbow[/b]. Just like we did in the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1691320/view/4112420334808949839][i]How The Guns in Hellbreach Vegas Are Tuned[/i][/url] - which some of the most avid readers among you might remember - we’re gonna be diving into the nitty gritty on what makes the crossbow tick!

Just like last time, this is going to be a more technical blog. We’re going to dive into the details of the various values that I’ve decided to tune the guns in Hellbreach to:
[list]
[*]Type
[*] Fire rate
[*] Damage
[*] Reload Speed
[*] Recoil
[*] Ammo Capacity
[/list]
[table]
[tr]
[th]Type[/th][th]Fire Rate[/th][th]Damage[/th][th]Reload Speed[/th][th]Recoil[/th][th]Distance[/th][th]Bonus Reward[/th][th]Ammo Capacity[/th][th]Ammo cost[/th][th]Weapon Cost[/th][th]Win A Weapon[/th]
[/tr]
[tr]
[th]Single Fire[/th][th]-[/th][th]300[/th][th]2.1[/th][th]0.3[/th][th]2000[/th][th]$0[/th][th]1 - 15[/th][th]$300[/th][th]$3,000[/th][th]Yes[/th]
[/tr]
[/table]

[h4]This one comes with a bang[/h4]
The crossbow is a unique weapon because each bolt is loaded with an explosive tip. You shoot, you wait, and… [b]BOOM! It detonates.[/b] Unlike its medieval ancestor, our crossbow, is a highly, modern and much deadlier alternative. But we’re not making it too easy: The challenge lies in the [b]slow reload[/b] speed. 

[h4]So how would I use it?[/h4]
The Crossbow is an interesting early game weapon that can truly help you out in a pinch. It’s great for dealing with larger groups of enemies, very similar to the grenade launcher. Where the grenade launcher will explode immediately, the slight delay on the explosive bolt will allow you to tactically manoeuvre before it detonates. This is also it’s strength. Shoot, reposition while reloading, detonate, shoot again. Before you know it the dismembered demons will be crawling around you, ripe for the picking.

I hope you found this interesting! Let us know if you’d be interested in getting more of these detailed weapon stats!

And finally, now we’ve gained some new followers since last time; Some burning questions that have been on my mind:

notes.title: FAQ: Answering Your Pre-Launch questions
notes.content:
[h2]Hey survivors,[/h2]

Ash here, the solo developer of the indie FPS Hellbreach: Vegas. Over the past few weeks, I’ve been receiving a lot of questions on Discord and in social media comments and I figured it might be a good idea to do [b]an FAQ write-up that’ll tackle a few of these questions: [/b]
 
[h3]Why Early Access?[/h3]
At this stage, Hellbreach has a full gameplay loop and plenty of hours of fun for you! However with this Early Access period, I hope to [b]realise its full potential[/b]. Additionally, since Hellbreach is an online game, it’ll remain an ongoing journey for me in which I dedicate myself to shaping the game and making it a great experience for both solo players and for friend groups looking for a new shooter.

[h3]Is it really a solo developer?[/h3]
Yes! The game is being developed by [b]me, Ashley Ellis, the one man development team behind Hellbreach: Vegas.[/b] Although I had assistance with models and animations in the initial stages, the majority of the game's creation has been my own work. In terms of actual game development, that aspect is entirely handled by me.

[h3]Is Hellbreach playable offline?[/h3]
Sure thing! Hellbreach Vegas is [b]playable offline in single player mode[/b].

[h3]Can I play Hellbreach in split screen mode?[/h3]
As a result of the game being playable offline, I've seen some confusion sparking up on Discord and social media. Unfortunately, the game [b]does not support split screen co-op[/b]. You can play with a team of up to 4 players, but only in online multiplayer using separate devices. 

[h3]Where are your servers located?[/h3]
The servers are located in: [b]EU (Germany), Canada, USA, Australia, and EA (Japan).[/b]

[h3]Does Hellbreach: Vegas have controller support?[/h3]
Originally, the game wasn't designed with controller support in mind, but it [b]has been made compatible.[/b] I'm eager to receive player feedback on the effectiveness of this controller integration.

[h3]When are you releasing the Early Access roadmap?[/h3]
The roadmap will be released on [b]Monday, March 11th in the Launch Blog[/b], so make sure to keep your eyes peeled for that! 

[h3]How long is Hellbreach: Vegas going to be in Early Access for?[/h3]
I aim for the game to be in Early Access [b]for approximately 6 months[/b], and I encourage you to check out my roadmap for a detailed overview on how I plan to spend this time. Of course, this will also depend on your input.

[h3]I am a content creator. Where can I get a key? [/h3]
Our Key distribution is done[b] via Lurkit[/b]. So please apply for a key there!

[h3]Where can I share feedback and report bugs?[/h3]
I mainly use [b]the Hellbreach: Vegas Discord server[/b] for feedback & bug reports! Click on our Discord banner below and let me know what you think!

[b]See you in Vegas,[/b]

notes.title: Play The Slots To Tempt Your Fate In Hellbreach: Vegas
notes.content:
[h2]Dear survivors,[/h2]

[i]“What happens in Vegas, stays in Vegas, so you might as well play the slots!”[/i]

As a careful reader, you may have already noticed [b]these lines on our store page[/b]. Slot machines are a core element of Hellbreach: Vegas — [b]and they can make or break a run[/b]. Will you get a great weapon, a powerful upgrade, or are you gonna gamble away your cash and come out empty-handed? Only the slots can decide your fate. 

In this blog, we’ll go over [b]the 5 slot machines in Hellbreach: Vegas and their unique uses[/b]. It’s important to know that Vegas is unpredictable, meaning that the slot machines change location every playthrough. That’ll keep you on your toes and make every run feel uniquely challenging. 

[b][u]So, what slot machines do we have in Hellbreach: Vegas?[/u][/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43190635/948e707d1568569ffd252de61215f7eaafb41793.png[/img]

[h3]'Win A Weapon' and sway your faith[/h3]
Possibly the most notorious slot machine, the Win A Weapon machine is the most RNG-heavy machine in the game. With 11 guns in its arsenal at Early Access launch, it’ll make you adapt your run based on the graces of Lady Luck. This will keep your run unique and make you use different weapons every time. For a never-increasing price of $3.000, this machine will keep you running back.

[h3]'Spin A Boost' for a power-up [/h3]
If you want to conquer an army that increasingly gets stronger, you’ll have to do the same. The core loop of your gameplay is scaling up on pace with, or faster than your enemies. The ‘Spin A Boost’ machine will do just that. 

This machine will quickly become part of your routine. It can reward you with up to 30% worth of extra damage each time you pull that lever. Though, it can also leave you disappointed by taking your money and giving you a juicy 0%, meaning you invested a lot and gained a whole lot of nothing. And that for an ever increasing price. It’s a true gamble. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43190635/9f6968a893ba472e21087624851f300ffee81f48.png[/img]

[h3]'Rand A Bang' for an explosive back-up[/h3]
When you start out in Hellbreach: Vegas, you’ll have 3 grenades that will help you out when you’re in a pinch. You’ll quickly realise, though, that they’ll prove quite useless as the round count increases.

The ‘Rand A Bang’ Machine can provide you with various unique grenades to resolve this for you:
[list]
[*] [b]Molotov[/b]: Burn, baby, burn. Disco Inferno! 
[*] [b]Ice[/b]: Aaaaand freeze! Just like that, everything stands still.
[*] [b]Vortex[/b]: The most convenient way to group your enemies.
[*] [b]C4[/b]: For that tactically timed ‘BOOM’.[/list]

[h3]'Bag A Prize’ for when you truly feel lucky[/h3]
You know that feeling. You’re just a few dollars away from that next boost? Don’t worry! Run the ‘Bag A Prize’ Machine and you might just get what you need. Stuff your pockets with a mountain of cash, or experience a gambler's worst nightmare and walk away with nada. 

[h3]'Pull A Skull' for your cosmetic needs[/h3]
We know you’ve been eyeing that beanie in the customisation screen. You know the one. The pink one with the pom-pom. Well, you’ll need skulls to get it. LOTS of skulls. Run the ‘Pull A Skull’ Machine to increase your end-game pay-out. Get some extra skulls to quicken your way to that new fresh look. You know what they say: Confidence is Key, and if those sleek ear flaps aren’t the way to confidence, we don’t know what is.

So. Are you ready to play the slots? 

Just 6 more days till you’ll find yourselves in an endless battle for Vegas.

notes.title: How The Guns in Hellbreach: Vegas Are Tuned
notes.content:
[h2]Welcome back survivors,[/h2]

I hope you held your ground in Vegas as the battle raged on. Once again, I want to thank all of you for joining last week’s playtest. I was able to gather some very useful information that’ll definitely be of help [b]when we move into Early Access on March 11th. [/b]

Today, I’m getting into some of the nitty gritty details behind Hellbreach. I’ll be deep diving into one of the most important aspects to keep in mind while working on an FPS: the weapons!

In this blog, I want to give you a short showcase of[b] how I tune your guns. [/b]
[u]
There are various values I’ve decided to tune the guns for: [/u]
[list]
[*]Type
[*] Fire rate
[*] Damage
[*] Reload Speed
[*] Recoil
[*] Ammo Capacity
[/list]

For the sake of brevity, I won’t be able to cover all guns in this blog, sadly. Instead, I’ll be covering some community favourites: the AK-47, the Mosin, and the M4!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43190635/c60c0552493371a4bc7ddc15a830c8b340b97b0c.png[/img]
[h2]So Let’s Analyse![/h2]

[h3]High Risk, High Reward[/h3]

While the Mosin may be tougher to use in dangerous situations - like, say, while you’re backed into a corner - it has high damage and a high bonus rewards for the kill shot. If used well, it’ll keep you in the running for most points obtained in a match. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43190635/a9b131742f61c76fec7318366049d1805b541040.png[/img]
[h3]The Devil is in the Details[/h3]
The M4 and the AK-47 may be very similar to each other in gunplay and stats, but the devil is in the details. If you look at the stats, you’ll soon realise the M4 is the superior gun in Hellbreach: Vegas. Where the AK-47 may serve as ol’ reliable for many thanks to their Counter Strike days, the M4 is faster, reloads quicker, has less recoil and offers a higher money reward as a cherry on top in Hellbreach. However, the ammo capacity is lower! So what will you do? Will you go for the extra ammo and the lower price-tag of the AK-47? Or will you start experimenting more with the M4?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43190635/32e58d1e4ec863e697137e8e9b00ef821fef88f5.png[/img]
[h3]The Meta[/h3]
Metas are a fickle thing and often just a matter of player preference. As I highlighted before, the Mosin is a gun that will leave you in the race for most points, and in our latest playtest we even learned about some new approaches with SMG’s… Yet, I’ve noticed that most people still try their luck on the Win a Weapon machine to get the minigun for example, because it’s known to be more versatile in tight spots due to its many bullets and high ammo count ([strike][i]Maybe an interesting one to analyze next time?[/i][/strike]).  

[b]So, what is your Meta?[/b]

I hope you found this interesting! Let us know if you’d be interested in getting more of these detailed weapon stats!

And finally, I’ll leave you with some burning questions that have been on my mind for a while:
What’s your favourite gun?
What gun did you get the furthest with?


Drop your answers in the comments below or on the Hellbreach Discord!

[h3]See you in Vegas![/h3]

notes.title: Hellbreach: Vegas - The Duality of Balancing Singleplayer and Multiplayer
notes.content:
[h2]Dear Survivors,[/h2]

[b]Welcome back, we hope you recovered from your weekend in Vegas. To cool you down after an intense few days of playtesting, we’re bringing you some light reading today. In this blog, we’ll be diving into the Singleplayer and Multiplayer elements which Hellbreach: Vegas has to offer. We will be taking a deep dive into how we balance them, and how we try to tailor them to each player’s unique preferences. 
[/b]
As we all know, there’s duality in gameplay experiences in the world of (wave-based) first-person shooters (FPS), between the thrill of a single person's achievements versus the banter and reliance of camaraderie in a Multiplayer game. Whether navigating the treacherous waves solo or banding together in a cooperative assault, our aim is to captivate you in both playstyles. Making both unique and fun to play.

Getting the balance right between a solo run and a team-up in Hellbreach was a bit like walking a tightrope – thrilling but tricky. The real game-changer wasn't about beefing up the baddies but getting the numbers just right. It's all about the spawn rates and how many of those neon nightmares we let loose on the screen at once. For the lone wolves, it's a manageable mayhem, but throw in a squad, and you've got a full-on demon party. Whichever style you play, it's the crowd control that makes all the difference in the end.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43190635/2d2cdab9c6c4d350be836f74464271514d5dba62.png[/img]
[i]image 1. So this is not how to position yourselves.. backed in a corner [/i]

[h2]So how has Ash tried to capture this magic in Singleplayer? [/h2]

Embarking on a solo journey in a wave-based FPS is a visceral experience. Whether you’re trying to have some fun, level up, or chase high-scores, you’ll be faced by a maelstrom of chaos and challenges. When you’re facing hordes of enemies alone, armed with nothing but your trusty arsenal, skill and strategy, your true mastery of Hellbreach: Vegas will be put to the test. Every decision is crucial, every shot counts, and the tension is palpable as wave after wave becomes progressively harder.
Ash has shaped Hellbreach in a way that the solo experience is an opportunity for players to truly get to know the game. The only person you can rely on is yourself, and as a result every mistake you make will be punished. 

Diving into single-player mode is thus like embarking on a personal quest for greatness. For Ash, it was all about hitting that sweet spot between a tough challenge and giving the players the rush of levelling up. You're in it to outdo yourself, round after round, getting a kick out of boosting your weapons and getting savvy with the perks. For many, the real buzz comes from topping your own best scores, pushing the limits to see how far you can go, and this is exactly what Ash set out to do. Solo play isn't just fun; it's about proving to yourself what you're made of, one demon at a time.

[h2]But I want to play with friends! How is it any different?[/h2]

On the flip side, the cooperative mode in Hellbreach: Vegas introduces an entirely different dynamic. The chaos that ensues is enhanced by your teammates being there, but also managed by their support. Teammates become allies in the face of adversity, and your success is no longer fully in your own hands.

Communication, coordination and sharing resources become paramount. While Singleplayer is focused on careful kitting, Multiplayer is focused on resurrecting your mates, communicating locations, and luring enemies to the various corners of the map to allow for the skillful completion of the round. 
For Ash, the key to Multiplayer was making sure it wasn’t too easy with additional players present. When switching gears to Multiplayer, the vibe changes. Sure, there's a bit of a competitive streak with those group scores, but it's more laid-back. Think of it as kicking back with your crew, mowing down demons while bantering over Discord. It's less about the scoreboard and more about having a blast with your friends. Multiplayer is where you chill, strategize on the fly, and share those "OMG, Did you just see that?!?!" moments. It's about that shared adrenaline rush and those belly laughs that come from taking on the apocalypse together. 

Of course that doesn’t mean we don’t expect dedicated squads to show us some true demon extermination SWAT strategies. The game will allow you to chase your chosen goals. Rest assured, the demons will be ready for you in Multiplayer too. In bigger numbers and longer waves.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43190635/778b349920fffdd92f73030e0beecf39d0e96487.jpg[/img]
[i]image 2. We weren't joking when we said 'in bigger numbers' [/i]

[h2]Why not both?[/h2]

We hope we have given you some interesting insights into what went into the design of both ways to play. As you try to get the most out of Hellbreach: Vegas, both modes will offer unique experiences. 

Bit of news for the dedicated readers; Ash is working hard to rework the leaderboard into Singeplayer & Multiplayer to reflect your achievements more accurately. If you get to round 30 in Singleplayer that’s a different achievement than in Multiplayer after all. 

[h2]So what will you be trying first? [/h2]

Will you test your mettle in solo mode, refining your skills and adapting to the ebb and flow of the waves? 

Or

Will you rely on communication and collaborative efforts and push for shared greatness in Multiplayer? 

We can’t wait to see how far you get.
[h3]
See you in Vegas!

The Hellbreach Team[/h3]

notes.title: Blog Post #2 - Demons & Sin City
notes.content:
[h1]Demons & Sin City
[/h1]

[h3]Introduction[/h3]
In this blog, we'll reveal the hellish inspiration behind the game's icy and imposing demonic army, and explore why Las Vegas was chosen as the perfect location for the battle with this demon invasion. From the city's reputation for vice and excess to its warm climate, every aspect of Sin City makes it the ultimate backdrop for this thrilling game. So, buckle up and get ready to take on the ghoulish invaders in Hellbreach: Vegas, where darkness and danger lurk around every neon-lit corner!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43190635/8a43df4fe88cd57357d8da6f73af0751d687f293.jpg[/img]
[h3]Where did the idea for Hellbreach’s unique demons come from and why was Las Vegas chosen as the setting for the game?
[/h3]

[h3]Ash:
[/h3]
Creating Hellbreach: Vegas has been such an interesting experience for me. It has felt like I was exploring both the spooky side of the supernatural and the lively atmosphere of Sin City. I was really inspired by the White Walkers from Game of Thrones and the Frost Giants from Thor. I just loved their icy look and how huge and powerful they were. That's why I decided to make a demonic army that had those same qualities, so players would have an awesome enemy to go up against.

The game's storyline revolves around the demons' desire to escape their dark and cold existence in Hell. With this in mind, I set out to find the perfect location for them to flee to, eventually settling on Las Vegas. The city's warm climate and reputation for vice and excess made it an ideal contrast to the darkness of Hell, providing an engaging backdrop for the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43190635/e0388fff48b1fc2f14ca823ee3636354bebdc77a.gif[/img]

Integrating elements of Las Vegas into the gameplay was an exciting challenge. The use of slot machines and perk cards had always appealed to me, and there was no better place to incorporate them than in the heart of the gambling capital. The bright neon lights and the thrill of the gamble became essential aspects of the game's art style, immersing players in the vibrant world of Sin City.

As players progress through the game, they will have the opportunity to test their luck with the slot machines and collect valuable perk cards to help them defeat the demonic invaders. The stark contrast between the dark, cold Hell and the bustling, warm atmosphere of Las Vegas not only enhances the gameplay but also adds depth to the game's narrative.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43190635/d5b89fcdebf72bfb864b4fb35ff86d42cf2457ec.gif[/img]

Developing Hellbreach: Vegas has been an interesting and fulfilling experience for me as a creator. I hope players will not only enjoy the gameplay but also appreciate the energetic gameplay and the environment that has been crafted.

In conclusion, Hellbreach: Vegas is a game that began with the influence of the icy White Walkers and the imposing Frost Giants, and it has evolved into a world where the fight against darkness is waged beneath the dazzling lights of Las Vegas.

notes.title: Blog Post #1: The Origins of Hellbreach: Vegas
notes.content:
[h1]The Origins of Hellbreach: Vegas
[/h1]

[h3]Introduction
[/h3]Welcome to the first installment of our blog series on the making of Hellbreach: Vegas. Here you will be able to find firsthand insights from the lead developer of the game himself, Ash. In this blog, we'll explore the origins of the game and the inspiration behind it.

To start this series, it feels appropriate to first start with a picture of the man behind it all! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43190635/fff81a014a0cc16c89092c01759d5c7f3c9178ca.jpg[/img]

[h3]Ash: 
[/h3]As a designer, I've always aspired to create immersive and engaging games. That's why, two and a half years ago, I embarked on a journey to create my first game, Hellbreach: Vegas. It was a daunting task, but I was driven by my love of gaming and my desire to create a game that I would love to play.
The inspiration for Hellbreach: Vegas came from my love of arcade-style shooters like COD zombies, Killing Floor, and Doom. I wanted to create a game that paid homage to these classics while also bringing a fresh perspective to the genre. I spent countless hours brainstorming ideas, designing characters, and developing gameplay mechanics.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43190635/27376d07df74d1b16db2c1e221f4a6705ad9ff14.gif[/img]

But game development is not just about coding and programming. It's about storytelling, creating engaging gameplay, and crafting an immersive world for players to explore. I had to learn how to design levels, create enemies and AI, and create engaging and challenging gameplay mechanics. It was a challenging and rewarding experience that pushed me to learn and grow as a developer.

As the months went by, I faced countless challenges and setbacks. There were times when I thought I would never finish the game, that I would never be able to create the game I had envisioned. But I persevered, and after two and a half long years of hard work, Hellbreach: Vegas is finally on its way to completion.

Launching a game is a nerve-wracking experience, and I'm still in the process of preparing Hellbreach: Vegas for release later this year. I'm excited to share my creation with the world, but also nervous about how it will be received.

Looking back on my journey as a game developer, I can't help but feel grateful for the experiences and challenges that have led me to where I am today. Making a game is a long and challenging process, but it is also one of the most rewarding experiences I have ever had.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43190635/acf925ef71243776ec2fd95f565aa3a37d211fcf.gif[/img]

As I continue to create games, I'm reminded of the importance of passion, dedication, and perseverance. Game development is not just a job, but a calling, a passion that drives us to create something exciting. And for me, that passion started with a simple question: could I create a game that I wanted to play? The answer, as it turns out, is yes, and I can't wait to share Hellbreach: Vegas with the world.

notes.title: The solo developer behind this wave shooter is trying to resurrect that old time CoD Zombies magic
notes.content: When solo developer Ashley Ellis told me that he wanted Hellbreach: Vegas to be a throwback, a celebration of the arcade simplicity of Call of Duty's beloved zombies mode, that's when it really clicked for me. Hellbreach is all about the simple pleasure of looking down iron sights at a zombie-adjacent demon-type dude and deleting it. If you find yourself doing so on a Discord call with three friends from high school, all the better... Read more.
